content.text:
**Finding: deviation — § 14.10 Assignment (p0188)**

The assignment restriction runs only against us. We keep an M&A successor carve-out and a "not unreasonably withheld" standard (so this is not walk-away territory), and no change-of-control termination or re-pricing right exists anywhere in the agreement. But there is no affiliate carve-out for our assignments and no restriction at all on IBM, which may freely assign — including to a competitor of ours. That asymmetry fails the fallback's mutuality requirement.

Redline (validated, ok:true) rewrites p0188 to: (i) permit Customer assignment without consent to an affiliate or to a successor by merger, consolidation, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets; (ii) retain consent-not-unreasonably-withheld for our other assignments; and (iii) mirror that consent requirement on IBM, with no assignment to a Customer competitor. The comment offers the mutual-notice fallback as an alternative.
